object_description: solitary three-level volume with generous platforms tempered by three patios and an atrium
geometry_property: free plan with freely arranged room groups
design_condition: the project renews the campus principle of a solitary set in an expanse of nature, but its three-level volume with a significant footprint struggles to find the breathing space that strategy requires

positive: The quality of the project is to offer generous platforms
Their depth is tempered by three patios as well as an atrium
Their appropriation is guaranteed by a free plan authorising an organic layout of the programme
This is capable of encouraging exchanges and meetings of users
It can be reconfigured during the operation of the building
The jury notes the interesting spatial potential of the proposed typology
The composition of the plan in a constellation of freely arranged small volumes generates spatial variability
This is desirable given the very great depth of the plateaus
The programmatic distribution is generally perfectible
The project is interesting from an energy point of view with good natural lighting
Solar protection is effective and light penetration through patios and atrium is satisfactory
The structural thinking is of quality and the post-slab system is interesting for flexibility
The construction is economical and the cost of the work is in the lower range
The same observation applies to the exterior fittings
negative: The bucolic vision avoids the question of whether the solitary-in-nature principle is still viable
The volume with a significant footprint struggles to find the breathing space required
It appears compressed by the existing context, generating residual spaces
It is far from the idyllic description given by the authors
The link with the avenue entrance is treated at a minimum
The project is very superficially contextualised, even in its graphic representation
The ground floor plan does not mention the exterior fittings
Some desires for formal composition contradict the conceptual proposal
The undulating facades make furnishing problematic
Non-standardised premises and secondary circulation positions freeze the plan
The landscape-like plan composition does not guarantee the evolution and flexibility suggested
Technical premises as hard points risk freezing the plan for a long time
Delivery access seems complicated and limited and the auditorium setup is impractical
The constellation risks disorienting users unfamiliar with the building
Patios could aid orientation if they were not used mainly for lighting offices
The ventilated double skin facade is incomprehensible and prohibitive for the energy target
Prestressed slabs contradict the versatility announced by the vertical structure
The undulation of the slab edges is closer to constructive mannerism than structural resolution
It induces complications and additional costs without objective advantages
The absence of glazing with openings is regretted
